title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, access setup (VPC peering, service account creds), and environment readiness for initial Redwood inference benchmarks. SE walked through benchmark outputs and tuning suggestions; security requested SOC2 artifacts and KMS notes. Next steps: provide credentials for staging, share security packet, run 1k-request benchmark next week, schedule a deep-dive on autoscaling and quantization options.
action_items: Maya Chen (Redwood) - Send latest SOC2 + security packet and KMS notes (due: 2026-10-16)
Samir Gupta (Atlas) - Provide staging VPC CIDR and service account for peering (due: 2026-10-15)
Jordan Patel (Redwood SE) - Run 1k-request benchmark and share results (due: 2026-10-21)
Priya Rao (Atlas) - Confirm data retention requirements and sign NDA addendum if needed (due: 2026-10-18)
next_steps: Redwood to share security packet and SOC2 audit link
Atlas to provide staging VPC/CIDR + service account credentials
SE to run performance benchmark at requested workload and share metrics spreadsheet
Schedule technical deep-dive on autoscaling/quantization next Wednesday
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-10-14 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~37 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Jordan Patel (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Atlas - Head of ML); Samir Gupta (Atlas - Platform Eng); Priya Rao (Atlas - Security)

Summary: quick check-in; onboarding mostly on track, one blocker for staging access; ran small set of bench results, some tuning suggestions from Jordan; security asked follow-ups re KMS and audit logs; next steps agreed.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Wednesday, um, we wanted to keep this short — last week we had the infra ticket open for the VPC peering, how's that looking, Samir?
[00:25] Samir: Yeah, hi. We started the peering request, network team replied that they need the Redwood peer CIDR and the service account to accept. I, uh, haven't put the service account together yet, that'll be tomorrow, I think.
[00:40] Lena: Quick note too, we want to make sure the staging region is west-us2, that's where our data lives.
[00:50] Jordan: Okay cool, that's fine. For the bench runs we did earlier I used west-us2 nodes to match latency. Results are in the spreadsheet I shared, link in chat - the 512-token median p50 is about 190ms on Redwood Dedicated 1xA100-ish config, with throughput around 18 rps. P95 is ~420ms.
[01:20] Priya: Sorry can you repeat the p95 number?
[01:23] Jordan: P95 is roughly four twenty milliseconds, so 420ms. There's some variance because we didn't have prefix caching warm.
[01:30] Maya: Right, we mentioned prefix/KV cache will help after warmup; Jordan, did you have tuning notes on batch sizes?
[01:40] Jordan: Yeah, so for this workload (short queries, mixed lengths) bumping batch to 8 improved throughput by ~18% but increased tail latency for single-request paths. If Atlas care more about latency for single user flows, keep batch at 1-2 and use caching on repeated prefixes. If throughput (throughput/ cost) is priority, batching and quantization look good.
[02:05] Lena: For our main app, latency matters for interactive clinician flows; cost matters but not at expense of response time. So we should target p95 < 300ms ideally.
[02:20] Jordan: Understood. We can try a config with small batches + warmed KV cache; that typically knocks down p95 by ~80-100ms in my experience. I'll include that in the benchmark run.
[02:35] Samir: Back to infra, the ask from network is they need service account IAM role details for the peering autopolicy, and also SAML metadata for the SSO side. We can provide SAML once we have the metadata.
[02:50] Maya: We'll send a template for the service account and the exact IAM roles. I'll also share the SSO metadata steps in case your IdP needs adjustments.
[03:05] Priya: Security here — we've reviewed the initial security brief but we need the SOC2 cert and clarity on key management. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys / KMS?
[03:20] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations. For the hosted/test POC we can provide encrypted at rest and show audit logs; for enterprise-grade key control we can sketch the guide on bringing your own KMS. I'll drop the SOC2 PDF and a short KMS note.
[03:38] Priya: Great, also, retention windows — we have 90-day retention policy for logs, might need to sync on log export.
[03:46] Jordan: We can configure audit log export to your S3 or SIEM; we have hooks in Redwood Console for per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns which might help.
[03:58] Maya: I'll include console screenshots in the packet.
[04:05] Lena: Regarding the benchmark, what load do you want us to mirror for production? We have two use cases: clinician interactive (bursty) and batch summarization at night.
[04:18] Jordan: For clinician interactive, emulate 1-2 rps per frontend instance with 95th percentile spikes to 8 rps for short bursts; for batch summarization, run a sustained throughput test at 50 rps for 10 minutes. We'll run both.
[04:32] Samir: I'll get the staging creds then; one more question is about private deployment — you mentioned Redwood Dedicated vs Private earlier — what's the recommended path for us?
[04:44] Maya: If data residency and KMS control are strict, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is the end state. Dedicated is our reserved capacity offering in our cloud with stronger isolation and SLA but not full customer-controlled keys. For POC we can start hosted/dedicated in a VPC peering setup and then evaluate Private if you need on-prem or bring-your-own KMS.
[05:05] Lena: Timeline wise, we prefer to have a decision point by end of month.
[05:10] Maya: Sounds reasonable.
[05:12] Jordan: Quick note on model variants — we ran the open model variant and also a quantized variant; quantized cut token cost ~40% with ~8% quality delta in our eval. Might be worth trying quantized in night batch flows.
[05:27] Lena: That's interesting. For clinician-facing stuff quality can't drop much, but for batch summarization it's okay.
[05:33] Priya: On the legal side, procurement asked about data processing addendum and whether Redwood can sign our DPA.
[05:41] Maya: We have a standard DPA and can do custom terms via our legal team; I'll attach the DPA stub.
[05:48] Samir: One blocker I want to call out — our staging VPC is currently behind stricter firewall egress rules; we may need explicit egress opening for the Redwood endpoint or use private link.
[05:59] Jordan: We support several connectivity options: VPC peering, private link, and on-prem connector. If egress is locked down, private link or a dedicated gateway is the reliable path. I'll add a short note on ports and endpoints.
[06:15] Priya: Can you also confirm encryption in transit? We need TLS and mutual TLS for some endpoints.
[06:22] Jordan: TLS is standard; mutual TLS is supported for Dedicated/Private setups — I'll add the mTLS steps to the doc.
[06:30] Maya: Okay, next up quick run through of the bench results spreadsheet, Jordan?
[06:36] Jordan: Yep. So sheet 'clinician-latency' — baseline (no cache) median 180ms, p95 420, as I said. With warmed KV cache median drops to 140, p95 320. With small batch (batch=2) + warmed cache median 150 p95 ~280 which meets your <300 target. So the sweet spot is warmed cache + small batching.
[07:05] Lena: Nice. Does that assume any quantization?
[07:08] Jordan: Those numbers were on the fp16 path. If we apply 4-bit quantization, you can get cost savings but p95 tradeoffs vary; for the interactive path I wouldn't recommend aggressive quantization. For batch summarization it's fine.
[07:22] Samir: The spreadsheet mentions GPU type as A100 and also an option running on T4 for cost baseline. Any rough cost delta?
[07:30] Jordan: T4 is about 30-40% cheaper but adds tail latencies; A100 is recommended for low p95 latency. We can provide estimated cost per 1k requests in the next benchmark run.
[07:44] Maya: I'll include a cost per 1k estimate in the follow-up.
[07:49] Lena: On the data side, we need to confirm whether prompts include PHI — some of our clinician notes might contain identifiers.
[07:58] Priya: Yes PHI is possible.
[08:01] Maya: Important flag. For PHI we recommend Redwood Private or encryption + strict retention and audit logging; for hosted POC we can enable additional redaction or tokenization before sending, and show you the logs. We'll include guidance.
[08:16] Priya: Also can we get an explicit list of audit log fields? We need to map to our compliance matrix.
[08:23] Jordan: We'll export field list. It typically includes request_id, model_version, timestamp, route, token_count, and trace_id; full payloads are optional and can be omitted.
[08:35] Samir: I'll add that to our compliance tracker.
[08:38] Maya: Great. Quick housekeeping: I'll send three items after this call — security packet (SOC2 + KMS notes), the service account template + IAM roles, and the link to the benchmark spreadsheet with the next-run params.
[08:55] Lena: Cool. For scheduling, can we slot a deep-dive next Wednesday?
[08:59] Jordan: I'm free next Wed 10-11am PT.
[09:03] Samir: Works for me.
[09:05] Priya: Works.
[09:07] Maya: Awesome. Any other questions or blockers before we wrap?
[09:10] Lena: None from me.
[09:12] Samir: No.
[09:13] Priya: Nope.
[09:14] Maya: Okay quick recap — Samir to send staging VPC details & service account; Priya to confirm retention and PHI handling; Maya to send security packet & DPA stub + IAM template; Jordan to run 1k-request and batch tests next week and share results; schedule deep-dive next Wednesday. We'll reconvene after benchmark. Thanks all.
[09:36] END: call ends

References/links mentioned: https://redwood.ai/docs/poc-onboarding (onboarding guide), https://redwood.ai/security/SOC2.pdf (security packet), benchmark sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/atlas-redwood-bench (internal), DPA stub: https://redwood.ai/legal/dpa_stub.pdf
